day_01_morning: ^You wake to the sound of a bell that should not be ringing.
^The Spire room is cold. Dust hangs in the light. On the sill, a cup of tea has gone entirely still.
^You do not know how you know. The words are already there, the way a bruise is already there.
^Mara Voss stands in the doorway with soot on her sleeves and her jaw set. Below the Spire, all of Aurel is holding its breath.
^If it rings again, the day starts over. You know that. You always know that.
^Mara holds out her hand. Above you, the Bell gives a sound like a tooth breaking.
hand: ^Good. We do this together, or not at all.
^Her hand is warm. The Bell cracks again, and somewhere below, a choir begins to sing.
^No. It is the Hollow Choir. It has come to finish the crack.
bell: ^The Bell hangs above you like a held breath. A hairline of white runs through the brass, bright as frost.
^Then stop counting and move. The Hollow Choir is already inside the wall.
day_01_afternoon: ^Ember Row is usually loud by afternoon. Today the stalls stand empty, their awnings ticking in the wind.
^Iven Sorn lowers his arbalest. He has the patient eyes of a man who has been counting exits.
^The Watch closed the checkpoint at noon. Said the ashfall was unhealthy.
^He tilts his chin toward the foundry. Black smoke is rising in a column that does not bend.
^Elias went in to fix a counterweight. He has not come out.
^The foundry gates are shut. Somewhere inside, something heavy is striking metal.
together: ^He checks his bow, then the door, then you. It is, you think, the closest thing to affection he allows himself.
alone: ^You go in through the ash door. The heat presses against your face like a hand.
^Behind you, Iven curses softly and follows anyway.
^You are going to get us both killed.
day_01_night: ^Night comes to Aurel the way water comes to a hull. Slowly, then all at once.
^Tomorrow the Bell rings again, and we begin again.
^The three of you sit beneath the great brass mouth. Somewhere in the city, a child is laughing. It sounds very far away.
^The Bell will take the day when it rings. You can anchor one thing against the dark.
warmth: ^You hold on to the tea, the soot, the two people beside you. It is not a grand memory. It is enough.
crack: ^You fix the crack in your mind: its whiteness, its angle, the exact note the Bell made when it split.
^Next time, we go straight for the source.
nothing: ^You let the day go. It leaves quietly, without ceremony, like a guest who knows they were never invited.
